q: Which of the following is NOT considered normal in a newborn?
e: Central cyanosis (blue tongue and lips) is always abnormal; the others are normal findings.

q: Which newborn finding is abnormal and needs investigation?
o: Skin dimple over the lower sacrum
e: A midline sacral dimple or hair tuft may mark spina bifida occulta: spinal ultrasound.

q: A newborn girl has bilateral breast enlargement with a little milk. The next step is:
e: Maternal hormone withdrawal; it settles in weeks. Squeezing causes mastitis.

q: All of the following reflexes are present at birth EXCEPT:
e: The parachute reflex appears at 8–9 months and persists.

q: At 36 hours a term baby has not passed meconium and has abdominal distension; X-ray shows dilated loops and scrotal calcification. The most useful test is:
e: Meconium ileus (with meconium peritonitis calcification) suggests cystic fibrosis: sweat chloride test.

q: A term baby weighed 3.4 kg at birth and 3.15 kg on day 3; feeding well. What is the best action?
e: Loss of 7% is normal (up to 10%); birth weight is regained by 10–14 days.

q: Which is given routinely to every newborn at birth to prevent bleeding?
e: Vitamin K 1 mg IM prevents vitamin K deficiency bleeding.

q: A newborn becomes cyanosed at rest and while feeding but turns pink when crying. A nasogastric tube cannot be passed. Diagnosis?
e: Newborns breathe through the nose; crying opens the mouth airway.

q: Which IMCI sign in a young infant needs urgent referral?
e: Movement only when stimulated is a danger sign of serious illness.

q: Bilateral absence of the Moro reflex in a newborn suggests:
e: Both sides absent: HIE, sepsis, kernicterus or drugs; one side absent: clavicle or Erb palsy.
